title: Marcos to Alex Eala: You remind us to be proud to be Pinoy
summary: President Ferdinand "Bongbong" Marcos Jr. on Tuesday praised Filipino tennis sensation Alex Eala for serving as a reminder for her countrymen to be proud of being Filipinos.

blocks.text: Published November 24, 2026 1:00pm
President Ferdinand "Bongbong" Marcos Jr. on Tuesday praised Filipino tennis sensation Alex Eala for serving as a reminder for her countrymen to be proud of being Filipinos.
Speaking at her homecoming event in Pasig City, Marcos told Eala, "We are not only proud of you, you remind Filipinos to be proud to be Pinoy, just like Hidilyn (Diaz), just like EJ (Obiena)."
Olympic gold medal weightlifter Diaz and former world No. 2 pole vaulter Obiena were also present during the activity.
"Pagka may kausap kaming hindi Pilipino, 'Ayan ang mga Pilipino. Akala ninyo kayo lang ang magaling? Magagaling din ang Pinoy,' and you make us proud to be Filipino," he added.
(When we talk to foreigners we say, 'Look at Filipinos. You thought you're the only ones who excel? Filipinos also excel,' and Alex you make us proud to be Filipino.)
Marcos also led the ceremonial serve at the venue's indoor tennis court, where he gamely engaged Eala, the No. 15 tennis player in the world, in a few friendly rallies that delighted the crowd.
Education Secretary Sonny Angara also tried his hand with the tennis racket against Eala.
Eala followed with a tennis demonstration to the Filipinos in attendance.
Grace in defeat
Marcos reminded the Eala, who was recently nominated as the 2026 Most Improved Player by the Women's Tennis Association (WTA), to take care of her body and avoid injuries to avoid permanent impact.
The President also pointed out that there's "grace" in playing sports.
"Other than injury, everything about sports teaches you good lessons, teaches you discipline, teaches you camaraderie, teaches you grace," Marcos said.
"Why grace? Kapag hindi ka nanalo, puwede mo pa rin lapitan 'yung nakatalo sa iyo and say congratulation na hindi ka nagagalit, hindi ka napipikon," he added.
(Why grace? If you don't win, you can still approach the person who won against you and say congratulations, where you're not angry or upset.)
The 21-year-old has climbed to a career-high ranking of No. 15 as of early November 2026, capping her season with a runner-up finish at the Hong Kong Tennis Open.
Be like Alex
Meanwhile, Angara urged the youth to be like Eala, who not only excels in sports but also finished her education.

"Gayahin natin si Alex Eala na hindi lang magaling on court, magaling din off court dahil alam ko masipag siya mag-aaral kaya naka-graduate siya, kahit na homeschooling siya, binibigyan niya ng oras ang pag-aaral niya despite all the demands of her professional career," Anagara told reporters.

(Be like Alex Eala who is not only good on the court but off the court as well. I know she studies hard that's why she graduated, even though she is homeschooled, she makes time for her studies despite all the demands of her professional career.)
Angara explained that it is important for Athletes to also finish their studies in order the prepare better for their retirement.
DepEd and Milo Philippines conferred the Gawad Sulo ng Simula at Tagumpay to Eala.
Angara said the award recognizes individuals with outstanding achievements.
"Definitely Alex has given a lot pride to the country," Angara said.

"It is really symbolic for Alex because Alex has already done so much for the country by just being Alex Eala and by being an excellent ambassador. So kapag mismong kausap na niya ang mga (So when she talks to) Pilipino on Filipino soil and encouraging them to play tennis, it's very hard to overstate 'yung impact nu'n, grabe," he added. — VDV, GMA News
